card.text: Explore the Moon in 3D with cssEarth. Discover impact craters, ancient lava plains, and the history of Earth’s natural satellite.

introduction.text: Earth's Moon records evidence of our solar system's history in the form of impact craters, cooled lava landforms, ancient ice deposits, and more.

surface.title: LROC photographic mosaic
surface.summary: Monochrome photography from 2009–2011. Crater shadows remain in the images; gray grid marks missing observations.

midnight-temperature.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: midnight temperature
midnight-temperature.summary: False-color temperature fitted to local midnight from 2009–2022 Diviner observations within ±70°. Gray grid marks unavailable data. This combines many nights, not current temperatures.

heat-anomalies.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: heat anomalies
heat-anomalies.summary: False-color difference from a typical-soil thermal model at slope-adjusted midnight, 2009–2022, within ±70°. Blue is cooler and red warmer; gray grid is unavailable. Residual terrain effects remain. Warm colors do not establish geothermal activity.

rock-abundance.title: LRO Diviner GHRM: rock abundance
rock-abundance.summary: Modeled rock-area fraction from 2009–2022 Diviner observations at slope-adjusted midnight, within ±70°. Gray grid marks missing or physically invalid values. This estimates rock area, not individual boulder counts.

topography.title: LOLA LDEM16 elevation model
topography.summary: Colors show height above or below a 1,737.4 km sphere. Shading reveals slopes in the archived laser-altimeter measurements.

crust.title: Crustal-thickness model
crust.summary: Thickness is inferred from gravity and topography. The result depends on assumed rock densities, not direct underground imaging.

silicate-signature.title: Diviner Christiansen feature, 2009–2016
silicate-signature.summary: Diviner measures a thermal-infrared emissivity peak related to silicate composition. This 2021 map corrects viewing geometry and space weathering. Colors span 8.0–8.5 µm; values outside that range share endpoint colors. This is a composition proxy, not mineral abundance; residual topographic effects remain, especially above 50° latitude. Gray grid marks missing observations and latitudes beyond ±70°.

geology.title: USGS unified global geology (2020 v2)
geology.summary: USGS interpreted geologic units from the 2020 unified map, version 2 (1:5,000,000). Colors distinguish mapped units and their relative ages; they are not photographed surface colors. Small units may be absent at this display scale.
